record.original_question: Call a C0-semigroup T on a Banach space X asymptotically analytic if there exist an analytic C0-semigroup S on a Banach space Y, a bounded linear operator P from X to Y, and, for every f in X, an element g in Y such that T(t)f = S(t)g + w(t) for all t >= 0 with ||w(t)|| = o(||S(t)g||) as t -> infinity. Which C0-semigroups are asymptotically analytic? As a first step, what can be proved in the special case Y = X and P = I, and more generally which C0-groups governing second-order equations and which non-analytic semigroups governing functional differential equations are asymptotically analytic?

evidence.quote: We call S "asymptotically analytic" if there exist S, P as above such that from all f ∈ X there is g ∈ Y so that T (t)f = S(t)g + w(t), t ≥ 0, where kw(t)k = o(kS(t)gk) as t → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $T = (T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ be a $C_0$-semigroup on $X$. Say that $T$ is asymptotically analytic if there exist a Banach space $Y$, a bounded linear operator $P\colon X\to Y$, an analytic $C_0$-semigroup $S = (S(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $Y$, and, for every $f\in X$, an element $g\in Y$ together with a function $w\colon[0,\infty)\to X$ satisfying
$$T(t)f = S(t)g + w(t) \quad (t\ge 0), \qquad \|w(t)\|_X = o(\|S(t)g\|_Y) \text{ as } t\to\infty.$$

(a) Characterize the class of $C_0$-semigroups on Banach spaces that are asymptotically analytic in this sense.

(b) As a starting case, characterize the asymptotically analytic $C_0$-semigroups under the additional restriction $Y=X$ and $P=I$ (the identity on $X$).

(c) Determine which $C_0$-groups associated with second-order abstract Cauchy problems are asymptotically analytic, and identify non-analytic $C_0$-semigroups arising from functional differential equations that are asymptotically analytic.
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of "asymptotic analyticity" as formulated here appears to be a recently proposed concept, posed as an open program asking for a characterization of such semigroups, with special subcases (Y=X with P=I, second-order Cauchy problems, functional differential equations) suggested as first steps. No published characterization theorem resolving the question was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial growth bounds and Fourier multipliers (arXiv:1712.00692)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies non-analytic growth bounds and asymptotically analytic C0-semigroups, but does not give a full characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Related concept exists but a complete characterization of asymptotic analyticity in the proposed sense is not established.
